target.title: fix(google-video): cancel unread response body on download error
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Added `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the throw in `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` error path, so the unread response body stream is cancelled and the underlying connection is released immediately.

**What NOT changed**: No change to any other provider (OpenAI, Bedrock, etc.). No change to success paths. No change to retry or timeout logic. No new dependencies.

Fixes #109978

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` receives a non-OK HTTP response (e.g. 403, 429, 500), the `response.body` readable stream remains unconsumed. Node.js fetch keeps the TCP connection alive until the stream is GC'd or read to completion, causing connection stalls and resource leaks.

**Root Cause**: Missing `response.body.cancel()` in the error path of `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` in `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.ts`.

**Solution**: Call `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing the error. The optional chaining handles null-body responses gracefully. The `.catch()` ensures the original download error is always thrown even if the cancel itself rejects.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0, OpenClaw 2026.7.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run the unit test suite to confirm existing behavior
cd /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/video-generation-provider.test.ts

# Run the dedicated evidence script that simulates body cancel scenarios
npx tsx scripts/evidence-video.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
=== HEAD commit ===
bb946de5cf8 fix(google-video): cancel unread response body on download error

--- Body cancel on error path ---
Body cancel executed: YES ✅
Error: Download failed: 403 Forbidden

--- Original error preserved ---
Body cancel attempted: YES ✅
Error: Video generation failed (500)

--- Null body (optional chaining) ---
Null body handled: YES (via ?.) ✅
Error: Bad request

--- All HTTP error status codes ---
Status 400: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 401: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 403: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 429: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 500: body cancelled=OK ✅
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All body cancel scenarios pass. The body is cancelled before throw for all HTTP error status codes. The original download error is preserved even when `body.cancel()` rejects. Null-body responses are safely handled by optional chaining without throwing.

**What was not tested**: Real HTTP fetch to an actual Google Cloud endpoint (the error path is hard to trigger without invalid credentials / rate limiting; the fix pattern is verified at the logic level).

## Tests and validation

```

      Tests  17 passed (17)
   Start at  07:10:38
   Duration  18.89s (transform 15.27s, setup 573ms, import 18.08s, tests 103ms, environment 0ms)
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary
